Brad Bradford.title: 105-109 Vanderhoof Avenue and 10 Brentcliffe Road - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
Brad Bradford.brief: City Council will decide whether to oppose converting 105-109 Vanderhoof Avenue and 10 Brentcliffe Road from employment land to mixed-use at the Ontario Land Tribunal. City staff recommend fighting it.
Brad Bradford.reason: The nature of my interest is that my wife is a planner on the file.

Brad Bradford.title: 2674-2704 Yonge Street and 19 Alexandra Boulevard - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
Brad Bradford.brief: Staff recommend approving a 13-storey seniors residence with 251 units at 2674-2704 Yonge Street and 19 Alexandra Boulevard, with 31 rental replacement units and a tenant assistance plan. City Council is asked to approve. The item also references $950,000.00.

Brad Bradford.title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds towards Public Realm and Streetscape Improvements related to "Manor Road Square" as prescribed in Official Plan Amendment 405 as a City-initiated Public Realm Move - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
Brad Bradford.brief: City Council is asked to release an extra $318,600 in development funds for the Manor Road Square public realm project.

Brad Bradford.title: 4888 Dundas Street West - Alteration of a Property Designated under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement - Request for Directions
Brad Bradford.brief: This is a confidential directions item: the City Solicitor seeks Council instructions on the heritage alteration at 4888 Dundas Street West.

Brad Bradford.title: 4884-4896 Dundas Street West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
Brad Bradford.brief: This is a confidential directions item: the City Solicitor seeks Council instructions for the 4884-4896 Dundas Street West Tribunal hearing.

Brad Bradford.title: 717 - 733 Mount Pleasant Road - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Ontario Land Tribunal - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, Seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
Brad Bradford.brief: City Council is asked to send its solicitor to the Tribunal over the refused variance at 717-733 Mount Pleasant Road.

Brad Bradford.title: 4884-4896 Dundas Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
Brad Bradford.brief: City Council is asked to oppose at the Tribunal the appealed 29-storey development at 4884-4896 Dundas Street West.
Brad Bradford.reason: as his partner is a planner on the file.

Brad Bradford.title: Our Plan Toronto: Recommendations on Forty-Five Employment Area Conversion Requests - Final Report
Brad Bradford.brief: Council is asked to adopt Official Plan Amendment 644 deciding 45 employment-area conversion requests.

Mike Colle.title: Toronto Transit Commission Infrastructure Capacity and Development - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
Mike Colle.brief: Addressing the gap between development approvals and unfunded TTC capacity as crowding worsens, goes to Council for a decision.

Mike Colle.title: Speeding Up the College Streetcar Study
Mike Colle.brief: Councillor Saxe asks the committee to get a Q1 2027 report on speeding up the College streetcar with transit priority measures.

Mike Colle.title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2026.TE32.25 - Spadina Road, between Lowther Avenue and Kendal Avenue - Toronto Transit Commission Subway Ventilation Equipment Replacement - Construction Staging Area - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
Mike Colle.brief: Procedural: council is asked to revise the Spadina Road construction staging plan for the TTC's subway vent replacement at Spadina Station. The motion also lists $2.00, $5.75 and $5 as additional listed figures.

Mike Colle.title: Improvement of Tactile Wayfinding in Line 5 Stations
Mike Colle.brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks Council to have the TTC work with Metrolinx on better tactile wayfinding for visually impaired riders at Line 5 stations, where tiles now lead only to elevators.

Mike Colle.title: It’s Time to Reinstate Cummer Station for the North York Centre - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
Mike Colle.brief: This motion asks council to seek federal and provincial funding to bring back the previously dropped Cummer Station on the Yonge North Subway Extension, to serve planned growth around North York Centre.

Mike Colle.title: Responding to Bill 98, Building Homes and Improving Transportation Infrastructure Act, 2026 - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
Mike Colle.brief: This motion asks council to endorse the TTC board's principles for staff joining provincial talks on a law that would give Ontario's transportation minister powers over regional transit fares and service rules.

Mike Colle.title: Towards a Vision for a Design Standard for Future Toronto Subway Stations - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
Mike Colle.brief: This motion asks council to have the TTC, the City, and Metrolinx study a design standard for all new subway stations, including platform screen doors, public washrooms, bike parking, and tall well-lit ceilings above platforms.

Mike Colle.title: Towards a Vision for a Design Standard for Future Toronto Subway Stations - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
Mike Colle.brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to develop a design vision for future subway stations as well-lit civic hubs with amenities and community space, pointing to examples like Taipei.
Mike Colle.reason: My son, Josh Colle, works for the TTC as the Chief Strategy and Customer Experience Officer and this report falls within his management oversight.

Mike Colle.title: Safer Subways: Making Public Safety a Priority and Restoring Confidence to Toronto Transit Commission Riders Across Toronto - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
Mike Colle.brief: Councillor Brad Bradford asks council to back subway safety measures: police in all subway stations, platform edge doors at priority stations, better cleanliness and lighting, station safety audits, and zero tolerance for harassing TTC staff. Ridership sits near 80 percent of 2019 levels.

Mike Colle.title: 2026 Operating and Capital Budget
Mike Colle.brief: This item is the Mayor's proposed 2026 budgets, which council must consider: an $18.86 billion operating budget and a $63.06 billion 10-year capital plan. It includes a 2.2 percent property tax increase. It cites a $1.8 billion 2023 shortfall, and plans $250 million from the Vacant Homes Tax and luxury homes tax for family affordability measures. The source tables cite hundreds of additional line-item figures not summarized here.

Mike Colle.title: Budget Implementation Including Property Tax Rates, User Fees and Related Matters
Mike Colle.brief: Approving the 2026 property tax rates for the 2026 budget, goes to City Council for approval. Taxes would rise 0.57% on average, and 0.70% for homes and industrial properties. Figures cited: $6,174,269,194.00, $74,996,117.00, $2,213,525,317.00, $4,223,129.00, $380 million, $75.0 million, $1,000,000, $700,000.00, $100,000.00, $120,000.00, $62,000.00, $7,274,452.00, $6,771,766.00, $502,686.00 and $500.

Mike Colle.title: Speeding Up Light Rail Transit and Streetcars - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
Mike Colle.brief: The City Manager, with Metrolinx and the TTC, would push ahead with green-light priority for trains at street-level crossings on the Eglinton and Finch West light rail lines, with an update in early 2026, if council agrees.

Mike Colle.title: Showing Respect for Transit Customers: Implementing a Toronto Transit Commission Money-Back Guarantee - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
Mike Colle.brief: A call on the TTC board for a money-back promise giving riders refunds when a trip runs 15 or more minutes late goes to council.

Mike Colle.title: Response to City Council Direction on EX.25.4 RapidTO: Transit Priority on Dufferin Street and Bathurst Street
Mike Colle.brief: This report follows up on the RapidTO transit lanes on Dufferin and Bathurst Streets. Staff are studying knock-on effects on nearby streets and would bring traffic-calming recommendations in early 2026.

Mike Colle.title: RapidTO: Transit Priority on Dufferin Street and Bathurst Street
Mike Colle.brief: Council would set aside bus-and-bike lanes on Dufferin Street between Bloor and King, plus bus-only lanes on other Dufferin and Bathurst sections, to make transit more reliable. The lanes would cost about $8 million, paid from the TTC's capital budget.

Mike Colle.title: Transit Priority Measures to Support Streetcar Service Diversions during King Street East and Church Street Intersection Closures
Mike Colle.brief: Council will vote on temporary transit-priority measures while the King and Church intersection closes for track work. Streetcar routes would be diverted from May to August 2025. The work would cost about $60,000.

Mike Colle.title: Transit Priority on Queens Quay East - Interim Priority Bus Lanes
Mike Colle.brief: Council would approve temporary priority bus lanes on Queens Quay East, Parliament, and Front Street West, to make transit faster for about 4,000 daily riders before the new light rail arrives. The bus lanes would cost about $800,000, paid from the TTC's capital budget.

Mike Colle.title: 2025 Operating and Capital Budget
Mike Colle.brief: This is the Mayor's proposed 2025 budget for Toronto, for council's approval: $18.849 billion in operating spending and a $59.597 billion 10-year capital plan. It starts with a $1.2 billion shortfall, a $600 million improvement from 2024's $1.8 billion, balanced with $680 million in reductions and offsets.

Mike Colle.title: Budget Implementation Including Property Tax Rates, User Fees and Related Matters
Mike Colle.brief: Council sets 2025 property tax rates and user fees, with an average tax-rate increase of 4.37%. The rates would raise a $6.063 billion property tax levy, including an extra $250.8 million from the budget increase and $69.7 million for transit and housing projects. The average home would pay $4,160 in municipal property tax.

Mike Colle.title: Updated Long-Term Financial Plan
Mike Colle.brief: City Council is asked to acknowledge a $46.5 billion 10-year fiscal gap and approve graduated land transfer tax rates.

Nick Mantas.title: Review of Toronto’s Street Vending and Artists By-laws
Nick Mantas.brief: Before Council for a decision: make interim changes to street vending rules, including new sidewalk food-vending permits in Wards 10, 11 and 13 and removing the five-hour vending limit. The report's dollar figures are $1,000,000,, $4,465.84, $2,429.07, $5,000.00, $2,500.00, $3,750.00, $512.66, $387.50, $258.33, $25.63, $250.00, $140.00, $65.00, $47.58, $25.08, $100.00, $200.00, $474.52, $351.16, $758.01, $370.08, $1,407.83, and $955.92.
Nick Mantas.reason: My family member operates a vending truck.

Nick Mantas.title: Proposed Pilot for Non-Motorized Mobile Food Vendors in University-Rosedale
Nick Mantas.brief: The street vending bylaw for a pilot allowing non-motorized food vendors, like food carts, in mobile vending zones in University-Rosedale (Ward 11) would be amended, if council agrees.

Nick Mantas.title: Mayor’s Economic Action Plan in Response to United States Tariffs
Nick Mantas.brief: Council would adopt the Mayor's economic plan in response to US tariffs, keep it updated, and report to the July Executive Committee on how it is being put into action. Staffing for the first steps would cost about $2.4 million, paid from existing budgets.

Nick Mantas.title: Extending Vehicle Age Limits for Vehicles-for-Hire
Nick Mantas.brief: Council would let wheelchair-accessible taxis and private vehicles be up to ten model years old, and let taxis and limos due for replacement by March 2025 keep running until August 2025.

Nick Mantas.title: Budget Implementation Including Property Tax Rates, User Fees and Related Matters
Nick Mantas.brief: Council sets 2025 property tax rates and user fees, with an average tax-rate increase of 4.37%. The rates would raise a $6.063 billion property tax levy, including an extra $250.8 million from the budget increase and $69.7 million for transit and housing projects. The average home would pay $4,160 in municipal property tax.

Nick Mantas.title: Analysis of Driver Wages in the Vehicle-for-Hire Industry
Nick Mantas.brief: City Council receives an analysis of driver wages in the vehicle-for-hire industry.

Nick Mantas.title: Uber Litigation Regarding Limit on Number of Private Transportation Company Driver Licences
Nick Mantas.brief: Council is advised that a confidential report on Uber's court challenge of driver licence limits is coming.

Nick Mantas.title: Transitioning the Vehicle-for-Hire Industry to Net Zero Emissions by 2030
Nick Mantas.brief: City Council is asked to require net zero emissions for vehicles-for-hire by 2030.

Frances Nunziata.title: ConnectTO Program Update: City Assets for Efficiency and Connectivity
Frances Nunziata.brief: City Council receives a ConnectTO update and is asked to direct consultation on next steps.

Jon Burnside.title: 1053 Don Mills Road, 2, 4, 4R, and 6 The Donway East Zoning By-law Amendment - Request for Direction Report
Jon Burnside.brief: This is a confidential directions item: Council is asked to adopt the City Solicitor's instructions for the Don Mills Road Tribunal hearing.

Jon Burnside.title: 1053 Don Mills Road, 2, 4, 4R, and 6 The Donway East Zoning By-law Amendment, Plan of Subdivision, and Site Plan Applications - Appeal Report
Jon Burnside.brief: Council is asked to oppose the four-tower, 1,185-unit development near Don Mills Road at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

Shelley Carroll.title: 1 Broadlands Boulevard - Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Decision Report - Approval
Shelley Carroll.brief: Approval of a three-storey building with 21 homes at 1 Broadlands Boulevard in North York is before council. Future residents would be affected.

Shelley Carroll.title: Broadlands Boulevard and Castlegrove Boulevard - All-Way Stop Control
Shelley Carroll.brief: North York Community Council is asked not to install an all-way stop at Broadlands and Castlegrove Boulevards.

Anthony Perruzza.title: 12 Hillside Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
Anthony Perruzza.brief: Staff recommend refusing the two-storey house proposed at 12 Hillside Road because the site is in a natural area.

Stephen Holyday.title: 2023 Write-Off of Uncollectible Property Taxes and Accounts Receivable
Stephen Holyday.brief: This is a finance item: Council is asked to write off $1.95 million in uncollectible property taxes.

Olivia Chow.title: 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
Olivia Chow.brief: City Council will decide whether to grow an approved College Street development from 31 to 45 storeys, raising the home count from 490 to 684, including 545 affordable rentals. The 2024 approval for the site's 408 affordable units carries a $27.7 million financial impact.

Olivia Chow.title: Chinatown Tomorrow Planning Initiative - Final Report
Olivia Chow.brief: City Council will decide whether to adopt the West Chinatown Planning Framework and related rule changes to guide future building, small business support, housing, public space and heritage protection in the area.

Olivia Chow.title: Chinatown Tomorrow Planning Initiative - Proposals Report
Olivia Chow.brief: City Council has the final say on whether to approve using a draft West Chinatown growth plan for public consultation, with final recommendations due in July 2026. The plan aims to guide growth while keeping the area's character and heritage.

Olivia Chow.title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - May 1 - September 30, 2025
Olivia Chow.brief: Council will vote on allowing listed festivals and events at Nathan Phillips Square from May to September 2025. These are routine event permissions.

Olivia Chow.title: 171 Pendrith Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councilor Parthi Kandavel
Olivia Chow.brief: City Council is asked to authorize an appeal of a Committee of Adjustment approval for minor variances at 171 Pendrith Street.

Jamaal Myers.title: Mayor’s Economic Action Plan in Response to United States Tariffs - Update to Council
Jamaal Myers.brief: Council would build a plan to protect and grow factory and industrial jobs in Toronto, report back by mid-2026, and bring options for the EDGE job-incentive program by late 2025. The EDGE program is worth about $1.9 million in tax breaks.

Jamaal Myers.title: Report on the Unauthorized Release of Confidential Information from a 2023 Closed Toronto Transit Commission Board Meeting
Jamaal Myers.brief: The Integrity Commissioner looked into a leak of private information from a 2023 closed TTC Board meeting and found no clear evidence a Board member leaked it. The Board is asked to accept the report and not penalize Chair Myers.

Jamaal Myers.title: Mayor’s Economic Action Plan in Response to United States Tariffs - Update to Council
Jamaal Myers.brief: Council would have the City Manager and Economic Development keep advancing the Mayor's economic plan in response to US tariffs, and report back to council in July 2025 on progress.

Jamaal Myers.title: Mayor’s Economic Action Plan in Response to United States Tariffs
Jamaal Myers.brief: Council would adopt the Mayor's economic plan in response to US tariffs, keep it updated, and report to the July Executive Committee on how it is being put into action. Staffing for the first steps would cost about $2.4 million, paid from existing budgets.

Josh Matlow.title: 11 Oswald Crescent - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
Josh Matlow.brief: The city's lawyer would go to the local appeals board to defend the refusal of a lot split and two new homes at 11 Oswald Crescent, if council agrees. The committee refused the plan in April 2025.

Parthi Kandavel.title: 5, 7, 9 and 11 Bellamy Road South - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
Parthi Kandavel.brief: City Council will decide whether to approve 110 townhouses, mostly three- and four-bedroom, at 5-11 Bellamy Road South.

Parthi Kandavel.title: 468 to 480 Danforth Road and 509 Birchmount Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
Parthi Kandavel.brief: City Council will decide whether to approve a 14-storey building with 526 homes and ground-floor shops at 468 to 480 Danforth Road and 509 Birchmount Road. The plan would also expand the nearby Sadler Parkette.

Parthi Kandavel.title: Declaring the Office of Councillor, Ward 25 - Scarborough-Rouge Park Vacant and Filling the Vacancy
Parthi Kandavel.brief: After Jennifer McKelvie's resignation, council declares the Ward 25 Scarborough-Rouge Park seat vacant and chooses between appointing someone or holding a byelection. A byelection would cost $550,000.

Chris Moise.title: Payment of Legal Expenses Related to an Integrity Commissioner Investigation
Chris Moise.brief: Paying back Councillor Chris Moise $20,807.61 for legal costs from an Integrity Commissioner investigation, under the council members' operations policy is on Council's agenda.

Chris Moise.title: Proposed Licensing Regulations for Animal-Related Businesses
Chris Moise.brief: City licensing rules for animal-related businesses like kennels, pet daycares and grooming salons, currently unregulated except for pet shops, would be created, if council agrees. Figures in the report include $2,000,000, $758.01 and $370.08. Running the new licensing system would cost the city about $293,500, mainly for extra staff.

Lily Cheng.title: RapidTO: Transit Priority on Dufferin Street and Bathurst Street
Lily Cheng.brief: Council would set aside bus-and-bike lanes on Dufferin Street between Bloor and King, plus bus-only lanes on other Dufferin and Bathurst sections, to make transit more reliable. The lanes would cost about $8 million, paid from the TTC's capital budget.

Rachel Chernos Lin.title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Hydro Board
Rachel Chernos Lin.brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel will interview six candidates and suggest three, including a chair, for the Toronto Hydro Board.

Dianne Saxe.title: 2 Whitney Avenue - Application to Erect a Structure in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
Dianne Saxe.brief: Council will decide whether to approve finishing a partly built stone wall on City land next to 2 Whitney Avenue in North Rosedale, which was built without a heritage permit. Staff now say the revised design fits the district's rules.
